brand.name: The Crisp Counter
brand.tagline: What to compare before you buy
brand.name_basis: Working brand adopted 2026-11-20 (decision D-P18) on the owner's standing directive that the site read as a polished, branded publication rather than a project codename; the name comes from the adopted design brief (DESIGN_PROMPT.md, warm-editorial direction). This supersedes D-P03's keep-'Prod2' stance for reader-facing surfaces; both sessions' rationale is preserved in the decision log. A preliminary name search on 2026-11-20 found no conflicting kitchen-appliance brand in the first page of results; a formal trademark clearance has NOT been performed and remains open as Q-19 with flag F-P21. Reversal is one line here + rebuild.
brand.mission: Three air fryers and two thermometers, chosen and explained by how you actually cook. Every figure is read from the official listing and dated; nothing is invented.

disclosure_sentence: As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.
disclosure_detail: Product links on this site are paid links (Amazon Associates Special Links). If you buy through them, the site may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Wording follows the Associates Program Operating Agreement §5 (S-OA), read 2026-11-20.
analytics_endpoint_note: Empty by default: the site sends nothing to any server until a self-hosted endpoint URL is set here and the site is rebuilt. Deployment of server.mjs is tracked as flag F-19.

editorial.voice: Warm, direct, practical. Take a position inside verified facts; address the reader; never describe the checking process as the story (D-12).
editorial.evidence_rule: Every published figure resolves to a dated read of an official listing or an official policy page. Prices and star ratings are not published (F-02). Popularity claims only as dated snapshots of an official page (D-19).

search_console.note: When the owner obtains the HTML-tag verification token from Google Search Console, paste it here and rebuild: tools/build.py emits <meta name="google-site-verification" content="..."> on every page. Until then no verification meta is emitted and no search-performance data exists.

reader_capture.consent_checkbox_text: I'm asking The Crisp Counter to answer this question on the site. If I left an email, use it only to tell me when the answer publishes. No lists, no sharing, no marketing.
reader_capture.note: The 'What should we answer next?' form posts to this URL only when it is set (any HTTPS endpoint accepting {"question": "...", "email": "..."}). While empty, a visitor's typed question stays in their own browser and nothing is transmitted. Before connecting it, settle the consent basis (Q-47) and update privacy.html.
